name: The Possession Demons of Aix / Loudun (Michaelis hierarchy)
note: Collective hub for the named possessing/expelled spirits enumerated in Sebastien Michaelis' Admirable History (Aix-en-Provence exorcisms of Madeleine de Demandolx, 1610-11), whose 'Pneumalogie' ranks the demons of the three angelic hierarchies. Attested only within this exorcism-treatise tradition.

name: Verrine
note: Demon of impatience named in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612) as a possessor at Aix; ranked among the second hierarchy, with St. Dominic given as his adversary saint. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Gresil
note: Demon of impurity/uncleanness in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the second hierarchy (Thrones), opposed by St. Bernard. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Sonneillon
note: Demon of hatred in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the second hierarchy, whose opposing saint is St. Stephen. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Carreau
note: Demon of mercilessness/hardness of heart in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the first hierarchy (Powers), opposed by St. Vincent. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Carnivean
note: Demon of obscenity/shamelessness in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the first hierarchy (Powers), opposed by St. John the Evangelist. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Oeillet
dom: breaking the vow of poverty; cupidity
note: Demon who tempts against the vow of poverty (riches/cupidity) in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the third hierarchy (Dominions), opposed by St. Martin. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Rosier
note: Demon of carnal love/seduction in Michaelis' Admirable History (1612), of the third hierarchy (Dominions), opposed by St. Basil. Attested essentially only in Michaelis.

name: Baalberith
note: In Michaelis' Admirable History (1612) the demon of blasphemy/quarrels, of the second hierarchy (Cherubim), opposed by St. Barnabas; later catalogues (de Plancy) make him the secretary/keeper of the archives of Hell. Derived from the biblical Baal-berith of Judges 8-9. HOMONYM: distinct from the existing Goetic spirit ENT_GOE_BERITH (Berith/Bolfry of the Ars Goetia), with which the name overlaps.

name: Titivillus
dom: scribal errors; idle/garbled words in prayer; the sack of dropped syllables
note: The medieval-to-early-modern patron demon of scribes' errors who collects mangled and skipped words from copyists and careless reciters of the Divine Office into a sack to be read against them at Judgment; attested from John of Wales / the Tractatus de Penitentia and later sermon and exemplum literature, surviving into early-modern demonology compendia.

name: The Witch's Familiar (familiar spirit)
dom: witchcraft; demonic pact; animal-shaped attendant spirits (imps)
note: Class hub for the low demonic attendant spirits ('imps'/familiars) in animal form (cat, toad, dog, etc.) said in early-modern English and continental witch-trial demonology (e.g. the Essex trials, Matthew Hopkins' Discovery of Witches, 1647) to be given by the Devil to suckle on the witch's mark and do her bidding. A class, not a single named being.
